feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain focus and solid public-sector experience. It shows breadth across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, which reduces impact and makes key achievements harder to scan.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong niche in digital platform modernization and communications systems leadership.  
- Good credibility signals: long progression at NACo, large-scale website metrics, named tools, and concrete platform examples add substance.  
- Broad but relevant skill mix: combines leadership, technical execution, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that fits senior digital roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and job bullets; several themes and tools appear multiple times. Consolidating would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond activity descriptions, especially in the freelance role; include measurable results where possible (adoption, efficiency, engagement, conversion, cost/time savings).  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly. No major misspellings found, but the footer project list is crowded and could be formatted more cleanly.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience; adding one or two concrete scale signals would make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce list-like stacking: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years building platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add scale/results drawn from recent roles, e.g. “Led modernization of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel noun phrase or first sentence continuation for smoother style consistency.
- Possible rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years modernizing public-sector web ecosystems, governance, and content operations. Built and led enterprise website, analytics, editorial, and multimedia systems—including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration, expanded reporting infrastructure, and AI-enabled search experiences—for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” closely overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The capability list repeats core competencies; keep the intro more outcome- and scale-focused.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into sharper, less overlapping capability areas with more consistent phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim filler: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations”
- Replace broader items with more distinctive strengths: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” is stronger than “content experiences”
- Clarify technical/operational scope: “Workflow automation and platform integrations” and “Multimedia production and livestream operations”
- Consider a tighter final version: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several phrases from the header (“enterprise web modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” “AI-enabled user experiences”)
- Overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; consider making this section broader and leaving tools/platform specifics elsewhere
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and skills. Tightening phrasing and making outcomes or scope more concrete would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and consistent style: “Created,” “Launched,” “Led,” rather than repeating “Built/Developed.”
- Clarify value where possible: mention audience, scale, or result (for example, improved policy discovery, supported campaign growth, extended conference engagement).
- Standardize wording and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI Hybrid Search” and “We Are Counties Microsite” substantially overlap with the current freelance role bullets.
- “Advocacy Video Series” closely repeats achievements already covered in multiple NACo roles; keep only if you add distinct scope or outcome.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project section. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and make the freelance/full-time nature feel more senior and strategic.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership language: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into fewer bullets focused on outcomes, e.g.:
- Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, including microsites, modular content components, and member-facing resource hubs.
- Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve cross-channel communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Directed AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI-enabled search and microsite details already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also overlap with the NACo role and headline summary.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and if channel management bullets emphasized outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a national membership organization.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Recast channel bullet to show business value: add engagement, growth, campaign support, or audience reach if available; otherwise shorten to avoid a generic responsibilities line.
- Combine operations/analytics language for concision: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role’s day-to-day channel management; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with “Advocacy Video Series” in Recent Projects; keep one focused on infrastructure, the other on programming.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as support-oriented rather than impact-driven. Tighten it to emphasize scope, ownership, and what expanded under your leadership in this period.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Replace “helping” language with ownership verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands…”; “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency across digital channels.”
- Add any measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, stakeholder teams supported, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier NACo role and the Recent Projects section; distinguish this as expansion/operationalization, not initial creation.
- “Publishing workflows/editorial coordination” also overlaps with the Director role; keep this version focused on execution rather than governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing like “audience-focused content planning.”

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for sharper executive-level positioning:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Content strategy for complex stakeholder audiences
- Consider replacing “messaging” with “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this area to scale from recent roles (e.g., 10,000+ page platform, 50+ publishers, millions of annual page views) rather than keeping it purely generic.
- Keep wording parallel: noun-based phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with Core Competencies; consider swapping in “content operations” or “stakeholder communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platforms list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items like “jQuery” unless central to target roles; it dates the profile.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages” to reduce bullet fragmentation.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, such as “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills broader and save full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating all three verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Power BI

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Consolidate tools into one phrase instead of a long list: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”

- Since recent NACo experience already proves these tools, avoid repeating the exact same platform list elsewhere unless this section is shortened.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to the in-house studio and event delivery leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding light qualifiers to show level: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep formatting parallel and concise; avoid mixing CMS names with broader capabilities here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry; consider trimming one or using this section for tools only and the topline section for broader capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus the seniority of the CV unless it supports a specific recent project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by function for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you actively use in recent roles/projects; if GTM is important, specify outcome-oriented use: “Google Tag Manager implementation”
- Suggested rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “API integrations” and workflow/technical execution themes also overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills; this section should stay tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”
- Keep only tools you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; cut weaker/older platforms if they dilute credibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack and Teams are very common; consider dropping one or both unless they support a specific systems narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize systems breadth, not repeat newsletter management.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/strength: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional scope instead of just names: **Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration, segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign deployment)**
- Keep to platforms only; avoid adding outcomes here unless you can tie them directly to hands-on administration or implementation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in recent work experience.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In Technical + IT, make it more tool-specific and trim broad capability terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • Google Optimize/VWO (if used)**
- Remove generic terms like **Dashboarding** and **A/B testing** unless you can name the platform or method; they read as capabilities, not tools.
- Move **SEO** to a phrasing like **SEO analysis** only if you want a capability here; otherwise keep this section strictly platform-based.
- If accurate, add one higher-signal implementation tool from recent work, e.g. **KPI reporting**, **event tracking**, or **tagging via GTM**—though GTM already appears elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping capabilities there and reserving this section for platforms only.
- **Dashboarding** overlaps with Looker Studio/Power BI and doesn’t add distinct value.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” and concrete contributions rather than general team support.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted through two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten and specify contributions: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; helped improve publishing workflows and cross-channel coordination.”
- Clarify standout outputs: “Contributed to a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email volume, or team size supervised.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; in this item, frame it as launching or early production support if accurate.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; keep this version more junior and execution-oriented.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while keeping scope modest relative to more senior NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize initiative and ownership: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Split the multimedia work into a clearer impact statement: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational campaigns and member-facing materials.”
- Make the podcast achievement the anchor: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If you can, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience/downloads, stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad phrases like “digital content production” if later NACo roles already cover multimedia extensively; keep this entry focused on research/innovation support plus the podcast first.
- Don’t overstate leadership here, since later roles more credibly show team and channel ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional-grade production tools and avoid repeating broader multimedia themes already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio production • Podcast recording/editing**
